common.purpose: Settle three I42 admission-application design points for Can: how functions that capture sql::pool through near satisfy mandatory assertions, whether each example program stays in one source file or splits into modules, and where each P13 outcome row is proven.
fixed_constraints: Four manifest-backed example programs (native-ai, account-search, form-validation, dashboard) each ship can.project.json, can.errors.json, src/, a README, and only declared assets and dependencies; each builds fresh, asserts real ordinary Can computation, and runs its documented interaction end-to-end from a staged release layout.

The P13 account-search contract fixes ordinary records, four named mounted callbacks, capture of one open sql::pool through the wrapper's near input, a static SQL descriptor, and an eleven-row outcome table; spec fragments plus test-harness behavior never count as complete source programs.

The current checker requires at least one assertion per function and binds each row argument to one non-elided input; http::request and sql::transaction inputs elide to a harness token, sql::pool inputs do not, and no Can expression constructs a pool value, so today no function taking a pool can be asserted.

Staged HTTP observes statuses, headers, and bodies while only the pinned browser observes HTMX swap and no-swap behavior; raw-provider and supplied boundary results stay labeled separately, and no live provider call backs any shipped verdict.

pool_assertion_inputs.background: The account-search production loader and its search callback take sql::pool through near, which the checker treats as an ordinary assertable input with no constructible value, blocking the mandatory assertions P13 demands.
facts: Eliding sql::pool would splice the same frozen typeless harness token the runtime already serves for every elided input, and any pool use the row does not when-supply fails closed at the denied live boundary.
No shipped fixture declares a pool input today: queries.can opens and closes pools inside function bodies, so widening elision accepts strictly new programs and renames no existing verdict.

The alternative is restructuring every callback to open and close its own pool per request, which keeps the checker untouched but contradicts the near-capture contract and churns one connection lifecycle per HTTP hit.

app_source_layout.background: Account-search spans records, the search_view model, HTML renderers, four callbacks, route mounting, boot, and main; the other three applications are smaller but share the same section mix.
facts: One src/main.can per application keeps every behavior in a single reviewable unit of roughly four hundred lines at the largest, with no cross-file provides or uses to keep aligned.
Splitting records plus model, renderers, callbacks plus routes, and main across src/ files exercises multi-file resolution, overlays, and navigation exactly as real projects use them.
Completion demands fresh builds, real assertions, and end-to-end runs either way; layout changes review shape and fixture realism, never the admission bar.

negative_allocation.background: P13's outcome table mixes query-validation 422s, SQL 503/500 mappings, route 404/405s, renderer failures, and shutdown behavior, each observable at a different boundary.
facts: Staged raw-HTTP runs prove statuses, headers, bodies, multiplicity, and limits deterministically, including every trigger row, but cannot observe whether HTMX swaps or withholds a fragment.
The pinned-browser harness proves 200 and 422 swaps plus 404, 405, 500, and 503 no-swap handling in a real engine at the cost of slower, heavier scenarios per row.
The I34 harness already aborts non-localhost requests and records per-check evidence, so browser scenarios inherit localhost-only proof and labeled results.

pool_assertion_inputs.instructions: Choose how pool-capturing functions meet mandatory assertions. Use common and topics.pool_assertion_inputs.

criteria.elide_pool: Elide sql::pool assertion inputs to the harness token, mirroring transaction handles: new programs check, no existing verdict moves, and unsupplied pool use still fails closed.
criteria.per_request_open: Restructure callbacks to open and close a pool per request with no pool inputs: the checker stays frozen while every HTTP hit pays a fresh connection lifecycle against the P13 capture contract.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot separate these designs, or neither keeps the required contracts.

app_source_layout.instructions: Choose the per-application source layout. Use common and topics.app_source_layout.

criteria.single_file: Keep one src/main.can per application: the whole behavior reviews as one unit and nothing cross-file can drift, at the cost of single-file-only fixture realism.
criteria.multi_module: Split records plus model, renderers, callbacks plus routes, and main into src/ modules: fixture projects look and resolve like real ones, with more provides and uses surface to maintain.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot separate these layouts, or neither keeps the required contracts.

negative_allocation.instructions: Choose where each P13 outcome row is proven. Use common and topics.negative_allocation.

criteria.split_by_observability: Prove each row where its observation lives: statuses, headers, and bodies over staged raw HTTP, swap and no-swap handling in the pinned browser; every row lands exactly once at its native boundary.
criteria.http_first: Prove every table row over staged raw HTTP and keep the browser to happy-path swaps: deterministic negatives with a light browser surface, leaving error-row swap behavior unproven in a real engine.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot separate these allocations, or neither keeps the required contracts.
